_doc: ISO-code and glottocode spine rows that share a display name while NEITHER source links them. These are the registries' gap, not ours: welding two rows because their names match would invent an identity no source asserts — the same move as picking a winner between disagreeing sources. Each pair stays until the sources link them; the red-team test re-checks the evidence every run, so an exemption SELF-EXPIRES the moment the ISO card gains the twin's glottocode, and a stale entry fails the suite instead of hiding a fixed bug.

pairs.name: Bhutanese Sign Language
pairs.why: dyl is a recent ISO 639-3 addition; Glottolog 5.3's bhut1234 carries no ISO code and the SIL table carries no glottocode.

pairs.name: Interlingue
pairs.why: the ISO card cites glottocode inte1260, a DIFFERENT languoid than Glottolog's inte1262 language row — the two sources genuinely point at different nodes.
